introduction: Targeted at high-yield JEE Advanced and NEET questions, this level analyzes the effects of dielectric insertion under different battery states, energy density, and the redistribution of charges between conductors.

core_concepts.title: Stored Energy & Energy Density
core_concepts.description: Energy stored in a capacitor: $U = \frac{1}{2} CV^2 = \frac{Q^2}{2C}$. The energy density (energy stored per unit volume in the electric field) is $u = \frac{1}{2} \epsilon_0 E^2$.

core_concepts.title: Dielectric Insertion (Battery Connected)
core_concepts.description: When a dielectric ($K$) is inserted while the battery remains connected: Potential ($V$) remains constant, Capacitance becomes $KC$, Charge becomes $KQ$, and Stored Energy becomes $KU$.

core_concepts.title: Dielectric Insertion (Battery Disconnected)
core_concepts.description: When a dielectric ($K$) is inserted after the battery is disconnected: Charge ($Q$) remains constant, Capacitance becomes $KC$, Potential drops to $V/K$, and Stored Energy drops to $U/K$.

core_concepts.title: Sharing of Charges
core_concepts.description: When two charged capacitors are connected, charge flows until they reach a Common Potential: $V = \frac{C_1 V_1 + C_2 V_2}{C_1 + C_2}$. This redistribution process always results in a loss of energy in the form of heat.

core_concepts.title: Electrostatics of Conductors
core_concepts.description: Under static conditions, the electric field inside a solid or hollow conductor is absolutely zero ($E=0$), and any excess charge resides entirely on its outer surface (Electrostatic Shielding).

important_entities.name: Force Between Capacitor Plates
important_entities.significance: The oppositely charged plates of a capacitor attract each other. Notably, this attractive force is independent of the distance ($d$) between the plates.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While the electric field inside a charged conducting sphere is zero, the Electric Potential is NOT zero. The potential inside is constant and exactly equals the potential on the surface: $V = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{Q}{R}$.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Minus for Same Polarity, Plus for Opposite
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Direct formula for energy lost during charge sharing: $\Delta H = \frac{1}{2} \frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} (V_1 - V_2)^2$. If plates of opposite polarity (positive to negative) are connected, change the term to $(V_1 + V_2)^2$.

exam_strategy_tips: If a problem states a capacitor is charged and then a dielectric is modified, your very first step must be identifying the constraint: Is the 'battery still connected' ($V$ is constant) or 'battery disconnected' ($Q$ is constant)? Do not proceed without this anchor.
